Series::log_normal_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series& Series::log_normal_() const
Series& Series::log_normal_(double mean) const
Series& Series::log_normal_(double mean, double stddev) const

What It Does¶

Overwrites every element of the receiver with exp(z) where z is a normal draw:

z ~ Normal(mean, stddev)
x = exp(z)

So every sample is strictly positive and the distribution is right-skewed. The catch is that mean and stddev describe the log-scale variable z, not the output x. For the output:

  • the median is exp(mean)

  • the arithmetic mean is exp(mean + stddev*stddev/2) — always larger than the median, and it grows fast with stddev because exponentiation magnifies the upper tail.

To target a desired output median m, pass mean = log(m).

Defaults are mean = 1, stddev = 2 (of the underlying normal). The one-argument overload sets mean and keeps stddev = 1.

Reproducibility¶

Deterministic given the process-wide RNG seed. Call pluss::rng_seed(seed) before sampling to fix the values; two runs from the same seed produce equal tensors. Each call advances a stream counter.

Parameters¶

mean (double, default 1): the mean of the underlying normal z. Must be finite.

stddev (double, default 2): the standard deviation of z. Must be finite and > 0.

Returns¶

Series& A reference to the receiver, now holding the samples. The write is in-place and preserves storage identity — every alias sees the values.

Raises¶

  • if the receiver’s dtype is not floating-point

  • if mean is non-finite, or stddev is non-finite or <= 0

Gradient¶

Not differentiable.

Examples¶

Example 1. Default parameters (z ~ Normal(1, 2)). Every value is positive; the tail is heavy. Seeded, so fixed.

pluss::rng_seed(42);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.log_normal_();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[6.5764, 5.8162, 5.1609, 70.2873, 0.3596, 0.9298]

70.29 in a sample of six is the right tail — with stddev = 2 on the log scale, that is expected.

Example 2. The parameters describe z, not x. With z ~ Normal(0, 0.5), the output median lands on exp(0) = 1 and the output mean on exp(0.125) ≈ 1.133.

pluss::rng_seed(7);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({500000}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.log_normal_(0.0, 0.5);
std::cout << "output median~" << x.median().host<double>()[0]
          << "  output mean~" << x.mean().host<double>()[0] << "\n";

Output¶

output median~1.00057  output mean~1.13324

The mean sits above the median — the signature of a right-skewed distribution.

Example 3. Non-floating receiver, stddev <= 0, and a non-finite mean are all rejected.

try {
  auto i = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);
  i.log_normal_();
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.log_normal_(0.0, 0.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.log_normal_(std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN(), 1.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

log_normal_: receiver must have a floating-point dtype
log_normal_: expected stddev > 0
log_normal_: expected a finite mean

Example 4. Reproducible under a fixed seed, and visible through aliases.

pluss::rng_seed(5);
auto a = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); a.log_normal_(0.0, 1.0);
pluss::rng_seed(5);
auto b = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
auto alias = b;
b.log_normal_(0.0, 1.0);
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "a == b: " << a.equal(b)
          << "  alias.is_set_to(b): " << alias.is_set_to(b) << "\n";

Output¶

a == b: true  alias.is_set_to(b): true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • mean and stddev are log-scale parameters. The output median is exp(mean); the output mean is exp(mean + stddev*stddev/2). Do not read mean as “the average value I want”.

  • The arithmetic mean grows steeply with stddev. A moderate stddev on the log scale produces a very heavy output tail.

  • Floating-point receiver only; stddev must be strictly positive.

  • Reproducible only after pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream.

  • Not differentiable.

Summary¶

log_normal_(mean = 1, stddev = 2) fills the receiver in place with exp(Normal(mean, stddev)) samples:

  • strictly positive, right-skewed

  • parameters describe the underlying normal: output median exp(mean), output mean exp(mean + stddev^2/2)

  • floating-point receiver only; stddev > 0

  • reproducible under pluss::rng_seed(seed); not differentiable; aliases see the write

See Also¶

  • Series::normal_: the underlying, untransformed variable.

  • Series::exponential_: a different positive, right-skewed law (with finite moments and a lighter tail).

  • Series::cauchy_: symmetric but heavier-tailed — and with no finite mean at all.
